# windowsddi_dns_mx_record_set (Resource)

Manages the MX (mail exchanger) records of one name in a zone, usually the apex (`@`).

The resource is authoritative for every MX record of its name: records of that name and type that are not in the configuration are removed. Creating it fails when such records already exist, so existing records are adopted with `terraform import` instead; dynamic records (registered by clients or the DHCP server) can be replaced with `allow_overwrite_dynamic`.

Updates are not atomic: new values are added first, then TTLs are updated, then old values are removed, so the name never resolves empty. A failure midway leaves a mix of old and new values, which the next plan shows and corrects.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# MX records at the zone apex.
resource "windowsddi_dns_mx_record_set" "apex" {
  zone_name = "lab.example.local"
  name      = "@"

  mx = [
    { preference = 10, exchange = "mail1.lab.example.local" },
    { preference = 20, exchange = "mail2.lab.example.local" },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `mx` (Attributes Set) Mail exchangers, one MX record each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--mx))
- `name` (String) Record name relative to the zone, for example `www`, or `@` for the zone apex. Case is ignored. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `zone_name` (String) Zone holding the records, for example `lab.example.local`. Case and a trailing dot are ignored. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `allow_overwrite_dynamic` (Boolean) When `true`, creating the resource replaces existing dynamic records of the name (registered by clients or the DHCP server) instead of failing. Static records are never overwritten. Defaults to `false`. Terraform only, not read from the server.
- `ttl` (Number) Time to live in seconds, applied to every record of the set (1 to 2147483647). When unset, the zone default is used on create and the server's value is reported.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<zone_name>/<name>` in lowercase, the import ID.

<a id="nestedatt--mx"></a>
### Nested Schema for `mx`

Required:

- `exchange` (String) Mail server host name, for example `mail1.lab.example.local`. A trailing dot is optional and case is ignored.
- `preference` (Number) Preference (0 to 65535); lower values are tried first.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import ID: <zone>/<name>, with @ for the zone apex.
terraform import windowsddi_dns_mx_record_set.apex lab.example.local/@
```
